title: E-Beam Inspection - Haze Detection on WaferSight PWG
subtitle: Post-Clean Quality Validation for 3nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Thomas Mueller

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the WaferSight PWG system to detect and classify Haze defects during post-clean inspection at the 3nm technology node. The test is conducted at Singapore Fab 7 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Haze defects that are critical to yield at the 3nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the WaferSight PWG platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: WaferSight PWG
- Inspection Type: E-Beam Inspection
- Target Defect: Haze
- Process Step: Post-Clean
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 3nm
- Fab Location: Singapore Fab 7

This test case applies to all WaferSight PWG systems deployed at Singapore Fab 7 for post-clean monitoring in the 3nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: WaferSight PWG
Software Version: v12.7.106
Recipe: E-BEAM_INSPECTION_3nm_POST_CLEAN
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: High (138 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 3mm
Sampling Plan: Full wafer sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the WaferSight PWG system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'E-Beam Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Haze defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 3nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 120 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 99% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.9% for E-Beam Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.93 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-05-17
Wafers Tested: 20
Total Defects Found: 536
Defect Density: 170.61 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 4.1%
Capture Rate: 92.3%
Test Duration: 226 minutes
System Uptime: 99.5%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The WaferSight PWG demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Haze at the 3nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Throughput metrics met production requirements without sensitivity compromise.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for Haze at 3nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
